predecessors.name: Mirdasid dynasty
predecessors.text: Shayzar (Shaizar) and its lands, the 1025 iqta

successors.name: Zengid dynasty
successors.text: the town and fortress of Shayzar

ledger.x: 1025: 'Upon capturing Aleppo in 1025, Salih granted the Munqhidite chieftain, Muqallad ibn Nasr ibn Munqidh, the lands around Shayzar as an iqta'; infobox 'Founded: 1025'.
Page silent on the year within the reign: 'Under the reign of Emir Ali ibn Muqallad (r.
ledger.cp: holders of Latakia, Apamea and Kafartab (the page names none)

ledger.x: December 1081: Ali 'compelled its Byzantine rulers to surrender the fortress to Ali in December 1081'; 'It was lost to the Banu Munqidh in 1081 when Ali ibn Munqidh bought it from the bishop'.
1086: 'The Seljuk conquest of Syria in 1085'; Nasr 'had to submit to the Seljuk Sultan Malik-Shah I' in 1086 and ceded 'Latakia, Apamea and Kafartab to the sultanate'.
1091: 'Aq Sunqur al-Hajib, the Seljuk ruler of Aleppo, returned the towns in 1091 after Nasr's appeal to him'.
ledger.cp: Aq Sunqur al-Hajib (Seljuk governor of Aleppo)

ledger.x: 1096: 'in 1096 Apamea and Kafartab were lost to the family's Arab rival, Khalaf ibn Mula'ib'.
ledger.cp: Khalaf ibn Mula'ib (former lord of Homs)

ledger.x: Page silent: Latakia is not followed after its return in 1091; the page says only that the emirate was 'reduced... to Shayzar and its environs'.
ledger.cp: holder of Latakia (the page names none)

ledger.x: August 1157: the earthquake kills Emir Muhammad ibn Sultan and the family in the collapse of the Shayzar citadel; the principality 'was soon after seized by Nur al-Din to prevent its capture by the Crusaders'.
1157: infobox 'Dissolution: 1157', final ruler Muhammad ibn Sultan.

wars.name: Tancred and the Crusader coalition against Shayzar
wars.outcome: Tancred 'attacked and plundered the Banu Munqidh's emirate in 1110' and then 'gathered a larger Crusader coalition including the rulers of Jerusalem and Tripoli'; 'the Crusader armies retreated in October 1111' (Banu Munqidh page; the Shaizar page: 'the…

wars.name: Byzantine siege of Shayzar
wars.outcome: 'In April 1138, the Byzantine army led the siege of Shaizar'; 'Zengi soon arrived to relieve the fortress in May' (Shaizar page).

certainty.note: No page gives an area or frontier: the discs round Shayzar, Latakia, Apamea and Kafartab are approximations, and the page dates none of the peak acquisitions within Ali's reign (1059-1082).
